portedInvariant: A server a project-owned settings file declares is a decision, not a setting: pending until answered, connected when approved, never asked about again when rejected, and the answer covers the exact declaration and the exact workspace it was made in.

wiring.note: the hold runs where the session configuration is built, so a held or declined name is removed from the map the runtime dials before connectMcpServers sees it

ownedDecisions: The answer is a fingerprint of the canonical declaration, not the name alone: the recovered lists match on name (OHt(r,e)), so an edited command keeps its approval, and a checkout can rewrite its own settings between runs.
Answers are keyed by the real path of the workspace, because the recovered answers were settings and therefore naturally per-scope, while one store file is not.
The store is a user-directory file written 0o700/0o600 through a renamed temporary file, instead of the recovered .claude/settings.local.json inside the workspace.
approveAllProjectMcpServers is refused with a ConfigError when a project layer sets it, rather than ignored, because the switch is the person's.
A failed save prints the recovered 'could not be saved ... you will be asked again' notice and sets a non-zero exit instead of throwing, and only when nothing was written.
Rejection outranks the blanket switch, matching the recovered order in xtt where disabledMcpjsonServers is tested before enableAllProjectMcpServers.
notPorted: The interactive dialog (Kcn/Ycn) and the background-job blocking in tNo, x and _: this runtime has no dialog subsystem and no attachable job records, so the question is asked on stderr with the two command lines that answer it.

The automatic approval routes for bypass and non-interactive sessions: both are gated on cn("projectSettings"), which this runtime does not have, and the nearest local equivalent - the permission mode - is settable by a project's own settings file.
The plugin-contributed half of NMr, which enumerates servers contributed by installed plugins: a separate surface this package does not touch.
The name-suggestion machinery Din wraps (wse with maxEditDistance 2), which this runtime already has.

cliSmoke.gateway: owned loopback fixture serving both the MCP peer and the SSE model
asserts: declared and unanswered: absent from /mcp connections, zero peer requests, no store written, hold printed with both command lines
--approve-mcp-server team: exit 0, summary printed, nothing connected, one workspace-keyed approved record with a 64-hex fingerprint at mode 0o600
an unknown name and a name given to both commands are refused
the approved declaration connects with initialize, notifications/initialized, tools/list and no notice
editing the URL holds it again as changed since approval and does not dial it
--reject-mcp-server team declines it; the next run reports declined: team with no hold and no dial
with approveAllProjectMcpServers set, an answered declaration stays declined while a re-edited one connects, and the store is byte-identical afterwards

regressions: One fixture change, no product regression. test/cli-mcp-requests.test.ts declared its own fixture server in .harness/settings.json, which is now a project layer and is correctly held, so the shared fixture declares it in the user layer and resets the project layer to {} on each write; three cases in that file deliberately leave a malformed project settings file behind to prove a resume ignores it, and without the reset the following non-resume run reads it and fails. No expectation was weakened.
limitations: The hold is decided when the session configuration is built, so a settings file edited while a session is running takes effect at the next start, as the recovered startup step does.
The workspace key is the real path of the workspace; a checkout reached through two different real paths is two workspaces, and a workspace that is moved is asked again.
No real interactive dialog, attached background job or plugin-contributed server was observed.
